passage: In his poem “The Second Coming” (1920), W. B. Yeats presents a world in which traditional order and restraint are collapsing, leaving the most committed people to be those with the worst intentions.
stem: Which quotation from the poem most effectively illustrates this claim?
choices: “The best lack all conviction, while the worst / Are full of passionate intensity.”
“Turning and turning in the widening gyre / The falcon cannot hear the falconer;”
“Surely some revelation is at hand; / Surely the Second Coming is at hand.”
“A shape with lion body and the head of a man, / A gaze blank and pitiless as the sun,”
steps: The claim has a specific second part: the worst people are the most committed.
Only the quotation contrasting the best (no conviction) with the worst (passionate intensity) shows that.
The falcon image shows loss of control but not who is committed; the others show expectation or a frightening figure.
key: Pick the quotation that matches the most specific part of the claim.
